texts.orig: ZnO films containing Er and Ge nanocrystals (nc-Ge) were synthesized and their photoluminescence (PL) properGe-containing film. Er-related 1.54 um emission has been investigated under several excitation conditions upon different kinds of Ge, Er codoped ZnO thin films. 1.54 um PL enhancement accompanied by the appearance of nc-Ge implies a significant correlation between nc-Ge and PL emission of Er3+ _ The increased intensity of 1.54 pm in Ge:Er:ZnO film is considered to come from the joint effect of the local potential distortion around Er3+ and the possible energy transfer from nc-Ge to Er3+ _ 2017 Chinese Laser Press

texts.orig: Doping erbium into semiconductors has attracted enormous interest in applications is within a wavelength range of minimum loss for silica fibers [1]. It has been reported that oxygen codoping and the use of wide-bandgap materials as the host material are effective to enhance the Er-related 1.54 pm emission [2,3]. ZnO is con sidered to be promising candidate as host material for Er doping because of an oxide with a wide bandgap of about 3.37 eV [4,5]. However; the efficiency of 1.54 pm emission in ZnO:Er thin films has not yet been satisfied. It has been con firmed that through the addition of Si nanocrystals (nc-Si) into SiOz, strong photoluminescence (PL) at room tempera ture could be obtained [6-10]. Ge nanocrystals (nc-Ge) have many properties (wide size-dependent emission tunability, larger Bohr radius, etc.), which is superior to nc-Si [11]. The lumines cence efficiency of Er?+ may be enhanced by the introduction of nc-Ge through the of local environment and recombination of photogenerated excitons in nanocrystals and subsequent energy transfer to optical optical being Er3+ change Er3+
